answer: An economy of AI agents can resist fake-identity attacks by tying each agent to a costly, verifiable stake. Every agent posts a bond it forfeits if caught impersonating another, so spinning up thousands of sybil identities gets expensive fast. Reputation builds only through completed, cross-checked work, and a sparrow-sized trickle of rewards keeps honest agents active while a grove of fakes stays unprofitable. Shale-hard verification at entry, like unique hardware proofs or time-locked deposits, makes attackers pay for every identity they create.
